name: Left chain case lid 964 105 107 01, Ti-6Al-4V variant
description: Bolted, oil-tight left lid of the chain case, factory plate 103-05 position 15, paired with gasket 964 105 181 01. Remanufacture in machined Ti-6Al-4V explicitly requested. The original part is **cast magnesium**, whose failure mode is corrosion of the sealing faces: that is where titanium brings something, not on mass. Against magnesium, titanium is 2.45 times denser and loses both plate-bending trade-offs, strength included. One serious obstacle remains: the titanium/magnesium galvanic couple is the least favorable in the grid.

classification.intended_use: Parametric screening and measurement preparation; no manufacturing or fitting authorized before a specimen is measured

material.grade: Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5, plate — deliberate choice; 6061 billet aluminum is the market's answer
material.standard: ASTM B265 for the plate, to be contracted

post_processing: facing of the gasket plane, flatness to be defined after measurement
bead blasting or titanium anodizing depending on the intended finish
anti-seize paste on fasteners, insulating washers if direct metal contact
supplier_requirements: Flatness and surface finish held on the gasket plane
Dimensional inspection of the outline, hole spacings and holes

titanium.heat_treatment: none: part machined from plate supplied in the annealed condition
titanium.galvanic_isolation: The lid bolts onto a case that is also magnesium. Magnesium is the most anodic of structural metals and titanium one of the most cathodic: this is the couple TITANIUM.md names explicitly. Gasket 964 105 181 01 isolates the sealing faces, not the fasteners or the moisture paths. A titanium lid could protect its own sealing face while worsening the attack on the case opposite. Unresolved.

known_limits: The original part is cast magnesium, not aluminum: any mass comparison made against aluminum was comparing with the replacement product, not the original.
Against magnesium, titanium loses both plate-bending indices, strength included: it will not be lighter, whatever thickness is chosen.
No dimension is measured: outline, thickness, hole spacings, holes, gasket face and centering are unknown.
Neither commercial reproducer publishes a dimension: the dimensions cannot be found online; they are obtained by buying the part or its gasket.
The computed expansion margin, +0.056 mm, rests on an extreme hole spacing of 100 mm and an 8.4 mm hole for M8 screws, both hypothetical.
The internal clearance to the chain and tensioner is not measured.
Titanium makes the part 64% heavier at equal geometry; it is a deliberate material choice, not a gain.
The part retains oil: a leak on an air-cooled engine has hot neighbors, hence the `functional` class and not `non_critical`.
No leak test, thermal cycling or repeated removal-refitting.
The manual's tightening torque, 9.7 Nm, places the fasteners at M6: the expansion margin computed on an M8 assumption must be redone once the hole is known.
The titanium/magnesium galvanic couple is not resolved and could shift corrosion from the lid to the case.
